messages:
Priya Nair: FYI customer CS-3412 reporting sudden 503/504 spike on hosted inference starting ~02:00 UTC. They see streaming responses cut mid-chunk and SDK retries looping back to our API. Putting initial notes here so we can triage quickly. Customer says it started after a high-traffic batch at 01:58 UTC.
Alex Kim: Can you paste a sample request ID and any gateway logs? Also what SDK and version?
Priya Nair: Customer SDK: redwood-js v2.4.1. Sample request-id: req_0a4f9c2b. Gateway error log snippet from edge-proxy: 
```
[02:03:12 UTC] req_0a4f9c2b upstream_response_timeout: downstream_conn_closed
[02:03:12 UTC] req_0a4f9c2b response_code: 504
[02:03:12 UTC] req_0a4f9c2b route: /v1/generate
[02:03:14 UTC] req_0b7d2a11 connection_reset_by_peer
```
Customer reproduces with concurrent streaming calls (n=40) and sees ~20% 5xx. They also attached SDK logs showing repeated 500/504 -> immediate retry -> same error (no exponential backoff configured).
Jordan Lee: That upstream_response_timeout + connection reset pattern looks like keepalive/connection pool exhaustion on the gateway. Did we change any LB or proxy keepalive settings recently?
Samir Patel: I pulled infra metrics for the window. There's a small autoscaler activity at 01:55 that drained 2 gateways, and connection count per node peaked. See short metric series: conn_count per node spiked from 1200->4200 for ~40s. Also CPU avg spiked to 85% on the remaining nodes. Could be that the pool couldn't handle concurrent streaming handoffs and timed out.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026 (auto) — priority P2. Linked services: edge-proxy, routing-gateway, autoscaler.
Alex Kim: Two parallel hypotheses: (A) gateway overloaded and started dropping/timeouting long-lived streaming connections, (B) a recent gateway config reduced max keepalive or per-connection limit causing earlier churn. Check config git diff for last 24h. If bucket (A) true, SDK retries are amplifying load and making it worse. We should ask customer to enable client-side jittered backoff / max retries=2 while we fix.
Priya Nair: Repro steps I used locally to reproduce (customer-supplied): 
1) Use redwood-js v2.4.1 with streaming generate.
2) Run 40 concurrent streaming requests (example using wrk or a simple node script).
3) Observe ~10-30% 5xx/stream truncation within 30s.
Sample curl for non-streaming repro: 
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-ggml-small","input":"short prompt","stream":false}'
```
Jordan Lee: I pulled gateway git and found a change 23h ago to the proxy: reduced max_keepalive_requests from 1000 -> 200 to avoid long-lived connections on older infra. That aligns with the timeline. Suggest temporary rollback of that change for hosted to see if it reduces 5xx during bursts.
Samir Patel: Also autoscaler aggressive downscale threshold bumped yesterday (scale_down_stable: 2m). If nodes drain too quickly during blips, connection redistribution causes transient overload. Recommend reverting that value to 10m for now.
Alex Kim: For immediate mitigation: 
- Roll back max_keepalive_requests to previous value for hosted edge (canary then global).
- Increase scale_down_stable to 10m.
- Patch SDK guidance: default jittered backoff and cap retries to 2 for streaming routes. Add server-side quick-fail 429 when we detect connection storm.
SupportJen: Draft customer update: 
"Hi — we’re actively investigating the spike you saw overnight. Preliminary root cause appears to be a change in internal proxy settings combined with a brief autoscaler activity that caused connection rebalancing. We’re rolling back a proxy setting and adjusting autoscaler stability. We’ll keep this thread updated and follow up with a timeline. In the meantime, you can reduce retry attempts in your SDK or enable jittered exponential backoff to minimize duplicate load. — Jen (Support)"

Priya Nair: I initiated a canary rollback of the proxy change at 03:10 UTC to 5% of edge nodes. Monitoring dashboard: error-rate on canary nodes dropped from 22% -> 1% in 3 minutes. Rolling to 40% now.
ops-bot: Deploy status: rollback-proxy-config v1.2.1 -> canary 5% succeeded, 40% in progress.
Jordan Lee: Confirming logs on canary nodes show keepalive request count returning to normal and the upstream_response_timeout rate falling. Good signal.
Samir Patel: Adjusted autoscaler config and bumped scale_down_stable to 10m at 03:22 UTC.
Alex Kim: Quick follow-ups for eng-runtime team: 
- Add circuit-breaker on gateway per-client-IP for streaming routes (threshold: >30 concurrent streams -> 429).
- Telemetry: emit a metric when keepalive reclaim happens so we can alert before 5xx spike.
- Short-term: enforce per-route max_concurrency to avoid single-tenant storms.
Priya Nair: Customer updated in CS portal with support draft at 03:30 UTC. They replied: "Thanks, please confirm when fully resolved, and we saw some billing oddities due to retries."
SupportJen: For billing: tagging BILLING-INV for investigation. Recommend we issue credits for duplicate attempts in that window once engineering confirms list of affected request IDs.
Alex Kim: Final note — ask customer to upgrade to redwood-js v2.5.0 once we cut a patch that sets default streaming retries=2 and adds jitter. I'll open a PR with the SDK change and a release note.
Priya Nair: Status update to customer posted at 03:45 UTC: rollback+autoscaler changes deployed to all hosts; error rates back to baseline; monitoring in watch for 2h. Will follow up with billing next steps. :thumbsup:
Jordan Lee: Marking thread for postmortem if incident threshold met. I'll collect traces and the config diffs.
Samir Patel: Leaving a reminder to run a replay of the customer's load against staging with the new settings to prevent regression.
ops-bot: INC-2026 updated: mitigated -> monitoring.
SupportJen: Customer acknowledged and asked for a short RCA within 48h. Assigning to eng-runtime + infra.
Alex Kim: Thanks everyone. If anyone finds lingering 5xx after monitoring window, ping here or escalate to P1.
Priya Nair: Closing thread for now; will reopen if we see new evidence.
